newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-MATTHAEUS WANTS END TO ROW AT BAYERN MUNICH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATTHAEUS WANTS END TO ROW AT BAYERN MUNICH.

text.p: Germany's most capped player Lothar Matthaeus on Tuesday sought to cool a dispute between himself and officials and other players at champions Bayern Munich. He said he was sure his future lay with the club.

"I hope and assume I will continue to play for Bayern. I value the responsibility and have a good relationship with the fans. It would be a shame if everything was to end in such a stupid way," Matthaeus told the Sport-Bild weekly.
The 36-year-old libero's statement came a day after Bayern president Franz Beckenbauer blamed the player for a public row between senior squad members and demanded he kept quiet.

Matthaeus launched a series of attacks on fellow players and club officials after he was dropped as club captain last month. He was stripped of the armband for publishing his "Secret Diaries", a behind-the-scenes look at Bayern's season.
Matthaeus said the row could be solved by talks with management and the players concerned. He was due to meet Beckenbauer for talks at the weekend.

"The final three months of last season showed how well I am in the position to work with the other players who were against me," he said in a thinly-veiled reference to his stormy relationship with Italy-bound striker Juergen Klinsmann.

New Bayern captain Thomas Helmer said he hoped Matthaeus could resolve his differences with team mates. Matthaeus had called for a public apology from his successor, who earlier described him as "sick".

"I don't have any problems with Lothar. But he must show he is really ready to sort this thing out. Because it is only when the team pulls together, like at the end of last season, that achievement is possible," Helmer said.
